extracted.intended_audience: mathematicians and prospective conference contributors/attendees (authors submitting abstracts/papers)
extracted.subtask_description: Compilation of submission guidelines, deadlines, and program-format requirements for multiple mathematics conferences (calls for papers, abstracts, and summaries). Useful for prospective authors preparing submissions and organizers handling program logistics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contributed papers submission deadline (Feb 15, 1993)
rubrics_metrics.description: Contributed papers should be submitted before February 15, 1993.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appears as a Call for Papers for the Clifford Algebras in Analysis (University of Arkansas) meeting: 'CALL FOR PAPERS: Contributed papers should be submitted before February 15, 1993.' Contact: J. Ryan or I. Monroe, Dept. of Math. Sci., Univ. of Arkansas, Fayetteville, AR 72701.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstracts: typewritten, ready for reproduction, ≤1 page
rubrics_metrics.description: Abstracts should be typewritten, ready for reproduction, and should not exceed one page.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stated as the submission format/length requirement (example: Algebraic Hyperstructures and other meetings). Also accompanied in some entries by a deadline (e.g., 'The deadline is May 1, 1993' for certain conferences).

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission: three copies of an unpublished paper in English; ≤10 pages
rubrics_metrics.description: Please submit three copies of an unpublished paper in English. The length of the paper should not exceed 10 pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Given as the Call for Papers requirement for MTNS 93 (deadline for submission of papers and proposals of special sessions: November 1, 1992). Contact/submission address: MTNS 93 organizers (details provided in listing).

rubrics_metrics.name: Three-page summary for proposed talk (call for topics)
rubrics_metrics.description: A three page summary of proposed talk should be submitted by November 15, 1992.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Listed under 'CALL FOR TOPICS' for the 'Number Theoretic and Algebraic Methods in Computer Science' conference and similar events. Used as the basis for topic selection; contact and mailing details are provided in the announcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: 300–400 word summary (one page) for prospective authors; submit three copies; deadline Feb 1, 1993
rubrics_metrics.description: Prospective authors are invited to submit three copies of a 300-400 word summary (one single page only) indicating one of the topics from above to which it should be assigned. Summaries must be received by February 1, 1993.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example from the First European Nonlinear Oscillations Conference: intended for assigning contributed talks; summary length and copy-count are explicit; contact and address details accompany the call.

rubrics_metrics.name: Talk durations and session formats
rubrics_metrics.description: Conference program will feature invited one-hour lectures and several invited half-hour lectures; there will also be sessions for 15 minute contributed papers. There will be invited and contributed talks, a poster session, and a problem session.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provided in conference program descriptions (e.g., First International Conference on Finite Fields; ICSTI event). Useful for authors planning talk length and for program organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract deadlines (various specific dates)
rubrics_metrics.description: Multiple conferences list concrete abstract/summary/paper deadlines (examples in this issue include May 1, 1993; February 1, 1993; November 1, 1992; December 1, 1992).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each conference announcement specifies its own deadline; authors must follow the deadline associated with the targeted meeting. See each conference entry for the exact date and contact information.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abstract formatting: ready for reproduction
rubrics_metrics.description: Submitted abstracts should be ready for reproduction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasizes that abstracts must be prepared in a form suitable for direct reproduction in conference materials (typewritten, clean formatting). This appears alongside the one-page-limit instruction in multiple calls.
